messages:
rachel: quick heads-up — onboarding samples are using mixed env names (REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY, RW_TOKEN). new devs hit 401s on first run and assume the service is down.

ken: ouch. is this from language forks?

iza: looks like it. node sample uses RW_TOKEN, python uses REDWOOD_API_KEY, rust example had SERVICE_TOKEN in the README. also noticed SDK retries on 401 which just hides the root cause.

rachel: proposal: pick REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY as canonical, keep REDWOOD_API_KEY as a 3-month alias, and retire RW_TOKEN. SDK should fast-fail on 401 (no token retry) and emit an `auth:invalid` event with a masked prefix and migration hint.

ken: agree. also add a startup warning when an alias is used so infra owners see the drift in logs.

ica: i'll patch samples and the README. i'll include a tiny integration test that runs `rw keys rotate --local` and asserts the env updates.

cred-lint-bot: flagged 4 files in PR #891: samples/node/index.js, samples/python/app.py, examples/README.md, docs/onboarding.md. recommendation: replace legacy names with REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY and add migration note.

cli-bot: rotation helper to include in onboarding: `export REDWOOD_SERVICE_KEY=$(rw keys rotate --local --json | jq -r '.key')` — paste into bash profile or use the wrapper script in docs.

ken: for SDK changes i'll add an `envPrecedence` helper, warning log on fallback, and a `strictAuth` opt-in flag for the next minor. default behavior will not change until we flip after telemetry. tests included (mock transport + no-retry assertion).

rachel: opened meta-issue https://github.com/redwood-inference/dev/issues/4201 with checklist: samples, SDK, cred-lint rule, docs. assigning tasks. thanks all — should make onboarding less painful.
